correctness.rationale: Every chosen structure is a point-hyperplane incidence reduct of PG(d,q), d>=3 and prime-power q>=2. For any two distinct points, exact counts for four incidence patterns of a fourth hyperplane are [m-2]_q, q^(m-2), q^(m-2), (q-1)q^(m-2), at least 3; the dual counts hold for two hyperplanes. For three distinct same-sort choices, independent triples admit all 8 opposite-sort patterns, while dependent triples admit the all-three and 3 singleton patterns, plus the all-zero pattern iff q>=3. These categories suffice for a four-move EF strategy, with equality, unary sorts and incidence preserved. The explicit rank-four three-point hitting sentence separates q=2 from q>=3. Minimum representatives have 30 and 80 elements. Standalone exhaustive recursive type checker computes identical roots for PG(3,2) and PG(4,2), distinct from PG(3,3); infinite proof is symbolic and does not rely on this finite evidence. A separate independent point/hyperplane table enumerator checks dependent/independent triple incidence supports for q=2,3,4,5, including the nonprime field q=4; its output matches the proved formula.

The related 2011 projective-space paper deals with incidence homology and modular GL representations; Venema handles modal projective-plane logic; a plane-specific result handles only dimension-two plane logic; related research records concern graph total-uniformity or unrelated rank thresholds. value.rationale: The theorem supplies a natural complete bounded-quantifier-depth invariant for the infinite, parameter-rich family of finite projective point-hyperplane incidence designs: all projective dimensions>=3 collapse at rank4, while field size has precisely a binary/nonbinary split. A geometric three-point hyperplane-blocking condition explains the first visible difference at rank4, and minimal 30/80-element representatives establish a sharp finite cutoff within this natural family. This does not depend on an arbitrary slice of a numerical table or a claimed downstream theorem.
